basic_info.name: Ambience Healthcare
basic_info.description: Ambience Healthcare is a US enterprise clinical AI platform that spans the full encounter lifecycle: a pre-visit suite (Patient Summary / Patient Recap, Chart Chat), an ambient scribe (AutoScribe) that drafts specialty-tuned, coding-ready notes from clinician-patient conversation, and post-visit revenue-integrity modules (AutoCDI coding/CDI, AutoAVS after-visit summaries, AutoRefer referral letters). The single most load-bearing fact for MediKiosk is that Ambience was the first ambient AI platform to ship a physician-facing pre-visit summary (Patient Summary, launched at St. Luke's in June 2025, expanded to Chart-Aware Patient Summaries in February 2026) - proving pre-visit clinician-facing summarization is commercially and clinically viable. Critically, however, it summarizes the patient's existing longitudinal EHR chart; it does not elicit a history from the patient before the encounter, and it is cloud-only, US-market, and (for note capture) English-only.

technical_features.what_it_does: Provides a connected documentation-and-coding workflow. Pre-visit: Patient Summary synthesizes the chart into a specialty-specific chronological or problem-based snapshot (each encounter reduced to 2-3 essential bullets, source-linked). During-visit: AutoScribe ambles an encounter and drafts specialty-tuned, coding-ready notes including a structured History of Present Illness produced from transcript plus chart context. Post-visit: AutoCDI surfaces ICD-10 and E/M coding with substantiation and audit trails, AutoAVS produces after-visit summaries, AutoRefer drafts referral letters, and a real-time compliance engine runs throughout. All output lands in the EHR workflow. It does not elicit a patient history before the visit; its summaries are grounded in existing chart data, not in patient-reported pre-consultation dialogue.
technical_features.architecture: Cloud SaaS built on proprietary, specialty-tuned AI reasoning models; its medical coding model was trained using OpenAI reinforcement fine-tuning (RFT). In August 2026 Ambience announced 'Chorus', a shared healthcare agent harness with a 'system of context' (navigates notes/medications/labs/admissions/diagnostics, reconciles contradictions, builds one source-linked understanding of the patient) and a 'system of action' that executes inside clinical workflows. Integration into EHRs uses native bidirectional APIs (Epic Toolbox/Ambient module, Oracle Cerner native APIs, athenahealth), reading chart context and writing structured documentation back.
technical_features.inputs: Encounter audio (ambient recording, sometimes requiring a ceiling microphone array), the patient's longitudinal chart (prior notes, diagnoses, labs, imaging, medications, pathology, problem lists), Epic CareEverywhere inter-organizational records, and patient inbox messages. Patient Summary analyzes 18 months of history on a nightly batch. No patient-facing intake questionnaire or patient-supplied document upload is described.
technical_features.outputs: Structured specialty-tuned clinical notes (SOAP and custom templates), a structured HPI, an assessment & plan grounded in current visit plus chart history, ICD-10/E/M code suggestions with audit trails, after-visit summaries (translatable for patients), referral letters, and pre-visit Patient Summaries (2-3 bullets per encounter, problem-oriented or chronological). Outputs are written into the EHR as documentation and discrete data - not emitted as an interoperable FHIR Composition/Bundle document.
technical_features.standards_compliance: US clinical-coding standards: ICD-10-CM, CPT, E/M and CMS documentation guidelines; coding quality is audited by the AAPC (96% E/M coding accuracy in primary care, 90%+ across 74 subspecialties, 93% ICD-10 substantiation). EHR write-back uses HL7 FHIR APIs in Epic (Toolbox/Ambient module) and Oracle Cerner bidirectionally. It does not claim or validate NRCeS NDHM/ABDM Implementation Guide conformance (OPConsultRecord, HealthDocumentRecord), HL7 IPS, SNOMED CT or LOINC as an emitted document, and no India/AYUSH terminology support exists. Compliance posture is HIPAA BAA, SOC 2 Type II, HITRUST infrastructure - privacy/security, not clinical document interoperability.
technical_features.offline_capability: None. Fully cloud-based SaaS requiring connectivity for chart access, inference and EHR write-back. No local storage, no on-device inference, no store-and-forward model. Pre-visit summaries run as nightly cloud batch jobs.
technical_features.languages_supported: Ambience states note capture is English-only today, with true multilingual documentation announced as 'coming soon' but not shipped; the AutoAVS after-visit summary can translate the patient-facing summary into other languages. Ambience's products page separately advertises a 'Translation for Documentation' feature that translates clinical conversations from any language into English in real time. There is no Devanagari note output and no Hinglish/code-mixed support. These claims are partially contradictory and the extent of multilingual handling is [uncertain].
technical_features.deployment_model: Cloud SaaS, enterprise deployment measured in weeks to months (third-party reports of 3-6 months, sometimes 6-18 months); may require optional recording hardware such as a ceiling microphone array; US-only confirmed customer base with no APAC deployments and no regional data-residency options outside North America. No kiosk, on-device or on-premise mode.

performance_metrics.accuracy_or_quality_metrics: Vendor and audit figures dominate: independent AAPC audits reported 96% E/M coding accuracy in primary care and 90%+ across 74 subspecialties, with 93% ICD-10 substantiation across supported specialties; a reported +0.035 (+29.3%) RAF increase across ambulatory primary care encounters (~$1.58M enterprise impact); and an OpenAI RFT-trained coding model reported to beat board-certified physician benchmarks by 27% relative (validated against 18 experienced physicians on complex multi-specialty cases). Operational claims: ~40%+ reduction in documentation time; roughly 45-57% less after-hours charting (Ardent Health reported 57%); Cleveland Clinic reported ~14 minutes/day saved on note-writing and chart review; MultiCare reported 92% clinician adoption and an NPS 63 points higher than the next-best solution; Cleveland Clinic onboarded 4,000 clinicians in 4 months with 70% sustained utilization and NPS 60. Several of these figures are vendor-cited or CFO-approved ROI rather than independently peer-reviewed; treat as [uncertain] beyond the AAPC coding audits and the npj-published Cleveland Clinic rollout.
performance_metrics.latency: Third-party reports cite roughly a 90-second draft time for a note [uncertain - not vendor-confirmed]. Pre-visit Patient Summary is not real-time - it runs nightly, analyzing 18 months of patient history and synthesizing each encounter into 2-3 bullets.
performance_metrics.resource_requirements: No local compute footprint - all inference is cloud-side; deployments may require optional ambient recording hardware such as a ceiling microphone array. Detailed local hardware/CPU/GPU requirements are not published. [uncertain]
performance_metrics.scale_metrics: Supports 100+ (and up to 200+) medical and surgical subspecialties. Named customers/deployments include Cleveland Clinic, UCSF Health, Houston Methodist, Memorial Hermann, MultiCare Health System, St. Luke's Health System, Ardent Health Services and Onvida Health. Reported ~$30M ARR (as of 2026) and a $1.25 billion valuation; more than 4,000 clinicians onboarded at Cleveland Clinic alone.
performance_metrics.evaluation_protocol: Combination of health-system head-to-head vendor evaluations (Cleveland Clinic's six-month pilot pitting five ambient scribes, after which it signed an exclusive five-year deal; MultiCare's 550+ clinician head-to-head), independent AAPC coding audits, a KLAS ROI study (St. Luke's ~$13,000+ saved per clinician annually), a peer-reviewed three-month study at St. Luke's reporting burnout falling from 45% to 31% and intent-to-leave from 31% to 18%, and an npj Digital Medicine / npj Health Systems paper on Cleveland Clinic's enterprise rollout (npj Digital Medicine 'Accelerating Ambient AI Scribe Enterprise-Scale Deployment'). Much of the financial/coding ROI is vendor- or CFO-reported; no independent peer-reviewed ROUGE/BERTScore/concept-recall/hallucination evaluation of note accuracy is published.

milestone_significance.relevance_to_module_c: Ambience is the closest deployed commercial analogue to MediKiosk Module C's pre-visit summary artifact, and therefore the most important prior art for it. It validates three things MediKiosk depends on: (1) that a physician-facing pre-visit summary is genuinely valuable and has measurable ROI and clinician-satisfaction impact, not just a nice-to-have; (2) that summaries should be source-linked, problem-oriented (with a chronological alternative), and concise (2-3 bullets per encounter); and (3) that summarizing historical record and highlighting what changed measurably reduces the dangerous copy-forward failure mode. It also exposes the precise gap MediKiosk fills: Ambience's pre-visit summary consumes an existing longitudinal EHR chart, so it provides zero value for the typical Indian OPD first-visit patient who has no digital chart - and does nothing to elicit that history from the patient. MediKiosk's Module C is the patient-elicited counterpart that manufactures the structured history Ambience would otherwise require to already exist.
milestone_significance.what_to_adopt_or_reject: Adopt: (a) the pre-visit summary as a first-class, dedicated artifact rather than a by-product of the scribe; (b) dual problem-oriented and chronological views, specialty-configurable; (c) strict source-linking / drill-down to underlying evidence - the commercial implementation of MediKiosk's per-field provenance; (d) the 'highlight what changed' anti-copy-forward principle, which maps directly to MediKiosk's repeat-visit delta summaries; (e) concise bullet-level synthesis (2-3 bullets per encounter) over verbose narrative; (f) outcome-based measurement (burnout, documentation time, coding/substantiation accuracy, utilization) as the pilot metric set; (g) the 'Chorus'-style shared, reconciled patient-context layer - but implemented deterministically and offline. Reject: (a) cloud-only architecture - Module C must run on a ~4GB CPU/iGPU kiosk offline; (b) English-only note generation; (c) US coding-standard-centric output (ICD-10-CM/CPT/E&M) - Module C must emit NRCeS FHIR R4 OPConsultRecord with SNOMED CT/Indic terminology; (d) proprietary opaque models and enterprise-only procurement; (e) reliance on the EHR chart as the source of pre-visit history - Module C must build history from elicited dialogue plus digitized documents; (f) writing into proprietary EHR fields instead of emitting a portable, validated FHIR document.
milestone_significance.limitations_and_risks: Its pre-visit summary is chart-dependent and therefore limited exactly where MediKiosk's target population is weakest: patients with little or no longitudinal record. Note capture is English-only today (multilingual 'coming soon'), and multilingual claims are internally inconsistent. It is cloud-only with no offline or edge mode and no India/APAC data-residency option. It is US-coding-centric (ICD-10-CM, CPT, CMS), with no NRCeS/ABDM or AYUSH terminology support. It emits EHR-native documentation rather than a portable FHIR Composition/Bundle, so there is no validated downstream FHIR summary artifact. Pricing is opaque, enterprise-only, and inaccessible to small practices; implementation is multi-month and may require dedicated recording hardware. Much of the headline accuracy and ROI evidence is vendor-reported or CFO-approved rather than independently peer-reviewed, and no independent hallucination/omission metric has been published. There is a risk of over-trusting the 27%-faster-than-physicians and ROI claims in a vendor-driven evaluation market.
milestone_significance.differentiator_vs_medikiosk: Ambience and MediKiosk occupy adjacent but distinct layers. Ambience is a doctor-side, cloud-hosted, US-enterprise platform that summarizes records that already exist and drafts notes in English against US billing codes; MediKiosk is a patient-facing, offline-first kiosk that manufactures the structured history where no chart exists, in Hindi/Devanagari and English, and emits an NRCeS FHIR OPConsultRecord Bundle for ABDM with physician attestation. Ambience strongly validates MediKiosk's pre-visit-summary value proposition but leaves MediKiosk's four differentiators (offline, India residency, NRCeS-conformant emission, patient-elicited bilingual history with per-field provenance) untouched. Its differentiator is eroding only in principle: if Ambience or a rival shipped offline multilingual FHIR-document summarization with India data residency it would compress the gap, but there is no evidence of that - Ambience currently has no APAC deployments, no data-residency option outside North America, and no ABDM/AYUSH support. Net effect: it strengthens MediKiosk's positioning while setting the quality and source-linkage bar Module C must meet.

business_info.license: Proprietary, closed-source commercial software; no open license.
business_info.pricing: Not published; all contracts custom-negotiated per clinical FTE. Third-party estimates put base AutoScribe at roughly $2,800-$3,200 per provider per year (~$233-$267/month), with the full suite (AutoCDI + AutoAVS + AutoRefer + AutoPrep) reaching roughly $4,000-$5,000+ per provider per year (~$333-$417+/month), plus a one-time implementation/integration/training fee; some estimates reach $300-$500+/provider/month. No self-serve plan, no free trial.
business_info.funding: $243M Series C closed 29 July 2025, co-led by Oak HC/FT and Andreessen Horowitz (a16z) with the OpenAI Startup Fund, Kleiner Perkins and Optum Ventures participating, at a $1.25B valuation; total raised approximately $373M (earlier Series B $70M in February 2024, Series A 2022).
business_info.commercial_status: Commercial venture-backed enterprise product; sold through enterprise procurement to US health systems only.

competition_ecosystem.competitors: Microsoft Dragon Copilot (Nuance DAX), Abridge, Suki, Nabla, DeepScribe, Freed, Commure Scribe. Ambience differentiates on coding/CDI depth and on pre-visit chart summarization; Abridge competes on clinician experience and valuation, Dragon Copilot on install base and Epic integration.
competition_ecosystem.integrations: Epic (Epic Toolbox membership since August 2025, Epic Ambient module, EPC Toolbox/Marketplace, CareEverywhere), Oracle Cerner (native APIs), athenahealth, using bidirectional HL7 FHIR APIs to read chart context and write structured documentation back. No ABDM gateway role (HIP/HIU/PHR), no Health Locker, no Indian EHR/HIS integrations.
competition_ecosystem.ecosystem_notes: The August 2026 'Ambience Standard' shifts the commercial model to value-at-risk performance contracts with embedded forward-deployed clinical/engineering teams, and 'Chorus' positions Ambience as an agent harness rather than a point scribe. The US ambient AI market is consolidating around a few well-capitalized vendors (Abridge at $5.3B, Ambience at $1.25B) with Microsoft price-cutting beneath them, driving outcome-based procurement. Critically for MediKiosk, Ambience has no APAC/India presence and no data-residency options outside North America, and the ambient-scribe category is not converging on offline, national-FHIR-IG document emission - so the India/ABDM/offline niche remains structurally open.

history.release_date: Company founded 2020 by Mike Ng and Nikhil Buduma; clinical products launched from around 2022. [uncertain - exact product GA date]
key_milestones: 2020 - Ambience Healthcare founded in San Francisco.
June 2025 - Patient Summary launched at St. Luke's Health System, described as the first pre-visit chart summarization technology from an ambient AI platform.
July 2025 - $243M Series C at a $1.25B valuation; company reaches unicorn status.
August 2025 - Ambience added to the Epic Toolbox program.
February 2026 - Chart Awareness expansion (chart-aware Patient Summary, A&P, Diagnostics, Coding).
history.recent_changes_last_6_months: (1) 12 February 2026 - Ambience expands 'Chart Awareness' across the platform: Chart-Aware Patient Summaries (problem-oriented longitudinal views), Chart-Aware Assessment & Plan (live, with chart-aware A&P in beta) to reduce copy-forward risk, Chart-Aware Diagnostics in alpha, and Chart-Aware Coding in early pilots slated for broad availability in 2026. (2) 19-20 August 2026 - Ambience introduces 'The Ambience Standard', an outcome-based partnership model that puts platform fees at risk against health-system targets (documentation time, coding accuracy, burnout, retention), powered by 'Chorus', a healthcare-specific AI agent harness (announced 24 August 2026) spanning 200+ subspecialties; cited outcomes include Ardent Health 3x validated ROI, 90% utilization and 57% drop in after-hours charting, Onvida Health ~$24,000 net annual value per physician, MultiCare 92% adoption and NPS +63, and a peer-reviewed St. Luke's study showing burnout down 45% to 31% and intent-to-leave down 31% to 18%. (3) August 2026 - an npj Digital Medicine paper documents Cleveland Clinic's enterprise rollout of 4,000 clinicians in four months with 70% utilization and NPS 60. (4) AAPC audits reported 96% E/M coding accuracy in primary care and 90%+ across 74 subspecialties, with 93% ICD-10 substantiation. (5) 8 September 2026 - Ardent Health CMO publicly frames scribe-only technology as insufficient versus Ambience's chart-reasoning. No India, offline, or multilingual-note-capture changes announced in the window.

market_positioning.target_users: US health systems, large group practices and revenue-cycle/CDI teams; 100-200+ specialties across ambulatory, emergency and inpatient settings. Explicitly not solo practitioners or small practices.
market_positioning.market_segment: Ambient clinical documentation plus coding/CDI plus pre-visit chart summarization - positioned as an end-to-end clinical workflow platform, not an intake/kiosk or FHIR-document tool.
market_positioning.positioning_statement: Markets itself as 'the only AI platform built for the full clinical workflow' and 'the AI transformation partner to the country's leading health systems', promising connected pre-visit preparation, real-time documentation and revenue-integrity, backed by the outcome-linked 'Ambience Standard' and the 'Chorus' agent harness; the core pitch is documentation, coding and CDI as one pipeline rather than three products.
